h: פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי מוֹת, ה׳ Acharei Mos, 5
The Bread of Torah Returns From Exile to Holiness

p: בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג ס, א)
In the holy Zohar (this parshah, III 60a):
from afar she brings her bread' (Mishlei 31:14):
from the head of the mind
that is, the thought of the mind,
is "the Torah came forth from Chochmah"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
and included in them is Torah she'b'al peh,
which is from the dew of Atika,
And earlier in the holy Zohar:
"'And she gives food to her household' (31:15):
'and he tears, and there is none to rescue.'"
that she tears away from the nations;
there is a vitality from words of Torah,
and that is the Torah she'b'al peh,
"And You give life to them all";
the Shechinah tears away from them.
For in the exile of Egypt
was the preparation for the giving of the Torah,
for then the words of Torah were
for then there was all the wisdom of Egypt;
only that the wisdom of Egypt
is a wisdom the Torah forbade,
the words of Torah were there in exile,
from the holy Arizal, of blessed memory,
that in the exile of Egypt were the souls
of the Generation of the Flood,
(בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, רטז, רֵישׁ ע״ב)
(in Zohar III, Ra'aya Mehemna, beginning of 216b):
in the Generation of the Flood,
but because they were wicked," etc.
which are the words of Torah,
וְכֵן הִיא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ל, יג)
And so it is in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah 30:13):
"The Holy One, blessed be He, wished
and it was decreed upon them,
And in the exile of Bavel
was the preparation for Torah she'b'al peh,
and so with all the exiles.
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת שְׁמִינִי, יא, ג)
and in the Midrash, Vayikra Rabbah, beginning of Parshas Shemini, 11:3):
"'She has hewn out her seven pillars' (Mishlei 9:1):
these are the seven books of the Torah."
and they are from the husk of Nogah;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חָדָשׁ, יִתְרוֹ, דַּף מב)
as it is written (Zohar Chadash, Yisro, p. 42),
where it lists the four husks,
כָּתַב נוֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, ד)
it wrote: "'And a brightness around it' (Yechezkel 1:4):
this is the kingdom of Greece,
around which there is brightness, etc.,
because among all the kingdoms there is none
to the path of faith like it."
there are some who attained through intellect
for they are only from the husk of Nogah,
and the brightness is not in them,
as written in the Zohar Chadash.
And this is what it says
בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (מְלָכִים א ה, י)
of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him (Melachim I 5:10):
the wisdom of all the people of the east
and all the wisdom of Egypt."
which he received from Hashem Yisbarach,
than the wisdom of the people of the east
and afterward he tore away from the nations
the vitality that is in them,
in the wisdom of the people of the east
And this is what it says,
his receiving and bringing out the vitality
from the wisdom of all the people of the east
and all the wisdom of Egypt.
And corresponding to the seven permitted wisdoms
Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, said
for they are only "vanity of vanities."
And this is what it said: "What is 'tereif'?
'and he tears, and there is none to rescue'";
the Shechinah tears away from the nations,
for it was with them in exile.
for the essence of Torah she'b'al peh
only that she also tears away
the words of Torah found among the nations,
for this is the vitality that gives them life;
of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
that he received his wisdom from Hashem Yisbarach,
and nevertheless he tore away from the nations,
the wisdom of all the people of the east,"
it says in the holy Zohar:
"'The heart of her husband trusts in her,' etc.:
the King to whom peace belongs,
that is, he trusts in her
that spoil will not be lacking;
what is taken as spoil from the nations.
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 130a):
like one who finds great spoil.'"
And how is milah alluded to in this verse?
But according to what was said,
that comes when attention is diverted;
the infant is circumcised at eight days
and through this he is included in
וּכְתִיב אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא)
and it is written, "Light is sown for the tzaddik" (Tehillim 97:11),
that he merits the primordial light,
which was hidden away for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh
only through the attribute of tzaddik,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קסו, ב)
as written in the holy Zohar (II 166b).
And this is what is written,
which is the Torah she'b'al peh
that is taken as spoil from the nations;
and this is through milah, as was said.
this verse is expounded about milah.
And we say this on Shabbos
for "and she gives food to her household"
refers to the eating of Shabbos,
which is "Come, eat of my bread,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג צ, א)
"'He gave food to those who fear Him' (Tehillim 111:5):
as it is written, 'from afar she brings her bread,'" etc.
And it refers to words of Torah
and to the eating of Shabbos,
which is also words of Torah,
And this is "from afar she brings her bread":
from the head of the mind;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סא, סוֹף ע״ב)
and as written (Zohar II end of 61b):
and this is the food "from afar."
And this is "and she gives food to her household,"
and it is written, "He gave food to those who fear Him";
is only for one who fears.
except Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
to fulfill the mitzvah of honoring a parent;
and through this his eating would be called
an eating of a mitzvah as well,
(in line with the reasoning of the Ran, beginning of the second chapter of Kiddushin).
And this is what it says (27:3-4),
and the preparing of the food
in order to fulfill the mitzvah of honoring;
and through this it would be "delicacies
that Esav was acting for the sake of Heaven;
and in truth he did feel in his eating
the holiness of the mitzvah of honoring,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not withhold
even the reward for fine speech.
And so in reward for the offerings
he merited that Rus came from him,
was not for the sake of the mitzvah
And this is what it says,
"He gave food to those who fear Him":
which is the eating of Shabbos,
and on Shabbos all of Yisrael are called
and they then merit the "food" and the "bread"
that she tears away from the nations,
and what she brings from afar;
